explanation.examTip: The test oracle provides the expected result; the test object is the thing being tested.

questions.questionText: Complete the sentences describing test types.

dropdowns.prompt: Testing that checks whether a system can be easily learned and operated by users is a form of __________ testing, a non-functional quality characteristic.
Testing that checks response times and resource usage under expected load is a form of __________ testing.

explanation.correct: Each blank is completed using the precise ISTQB CTFL terminology.
explanation.incorrect: Re-check the definitions in the syllabus glossary for these terms.
explanation.examTip: Both usability and performance testing are non-functional test types tied to specific ISO 25010 quality characteristics.

questions.questionText: For each statement about test levels, decide whether it is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: Component testing is always performed exclusively by an independent test team, never by developers.
System testing evaluates the end-to-end behavior of the fully integrated system against specified requirements.
Acceptance testing is only ever performed after system testing is fully complete and signed off.
Test levels can overlap and their exact activities can vary across organizations and lifecycle models.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: In practice, developers frequently perform component testing themselves, and acceptance activities can start earlier in Agile contexts.

questions.scenarioText: A development team has configured their CI/CD pipeline so that every code commit automatically triggers a build plus a suite of automated component and integration tests, with results visible within minutes.
questions.questionText: A team practices continuous integration where every code commit triggers an automated build and a suite of component and integration tests. Decide whether each statement about this scenario is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: This practice is an example of shift-left testing.
Automated component and integration tests running on every commit exemplify continuous testing.
This approach removes the need for any system or acceptance level testing.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: Continuous integration with automated low-level tests complements, but does not replace, higher test levels like system and acceptance testing.

questions.questionText: Complete the sentences about static testing benefits.

dropdowns.prompt: Because static testing does not require executing code, it can be used to find defects __________ in the development lifecycle than dynamic testing.
Static testing can improve __________, since consistent terminology and understanding are established through review discussions.

explanation.correct: Each blank is completed using the precise ISTQB CTFL terminology.
explanation.incorrect: Re-check the definitions in the syllabus glossary for these terms.
explanation.examTip: Early defect detection and improved team communication are two key benefits of static testing highlighted in the syllabus.

questions.questionText: For each statement about the benefits of static testing, decide whether it is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: Static testing can detect defects that are hard to find through dynamic testing, such as unreachable code.
Static testing eliminates the need for any dynamic testing later in the project.
Reviews can help detect defects in requirements before any code is written.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: Static and dynamic testing are complementary, not substitutes for one another.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are typical success factors for an effective review process? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Clear objectives are defined for each review
Reviewers are given adequate time to prepare individually before the meeting
The review focuses on criticizing the author personally rather than the work product
Defects found are logged and tracked to closure

explanation.correct: Clear objectives, adequate preparation time, and tracking defects to closure are recognized review success factors.
explanation.incorrect: Criticizing the author personally undermines psychological safety and is explicitly discouraged â€” reviews should focus on the work product.
explanation.examTip: Success factors for reviews mirror general psychology-of-testing principles: focus on the product, not the person.

questions.questionText: Complete the sentences describing coverage in white-box testing.

dropdowns.prompt: The percentage of executable statements that have been exercised by a test suite is called __________ coverage.
The percentage of decision outcomes (true/false branches) that have been exercised by a test suite is called __________ coverage.

explanation.correct: Each blank is completed using the precise ISTQB CTFL terminology.
explanation.incorrect: Re-check the definitions in the syllabus glossary for these terms.
explanation.examTip: Statement coverage and branch/decision coverage are the two structure-based coverage metrics in the CTFL syllabus.

questions.questionText: For each statement about equivalence partitioning, decide whether it is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: Every partition should contain at least one representative value that is tested.
Equivalence partitions can apply to outputs and internal values, not only inputs.
A valid partition and an invalid partition can never be adjacent to each other.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: Valid and invalid partitions are frequently adjacent â€” the boundary between them is exactly what boundary value analysis targets.

questions.scenarioText: An online store offers free shipping for orders totaling $50 or more, and an additional 10% discount for orders totaling $200 or more. These two conditions apply independently of each other.
questions.questionText: An online store gives free shipping for orders of $50 or more, and a 10% discount for orders of $200 or more (both apply independently). Decide whether each statement about testing this rule is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: Testing an order of exactly $50 tests a boundary value for the free shipping rule.
Testing an order of $200 alone is sufficient to verify both the free shipping and discount rules work correctly together.
A decision table could be used to systematically test the combination of the two independent discount conditions.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: A single test at $200 does confirm both individual thresholds are met, but does not by itself verify all combinations (e.g., an order below $50, an order between $50-$199, etc.) â€” a decision table would ensure combinations are systematically covered.

questions.questionText: Which of the following factors typically influence the estimated effort required for testing? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Complexity of the product to be tested
Skills and experience level of the test team
The quality of the test basis (e.g., requirements)
The color of the project logo

explanation.correct: Product complexity, team skill/experience, and test basis quality are all recognized factors influencing test effort estimation.
explanation.incorrect: A project logo's color has no bearing on test estimation and is an irrelevant distractor.
explanation.examTip: Estimation factors span product characteristics, process factors, and people factors.

questions.questionText: Complete the sentences about test progress monitoring and reporting.

dropdowns.prompt: A document produced during testing that summarizes progress against the test plan, such as tests executed and defects found so far, is called a test __________ report.
A document produced at the end of a test level or project, summarizing the testing performed and lessons learned, is called a test __________ report.

explanation.correct: Each blank is completed using the precise ISTQB CTFL terminology.
explanation.incorrect: Re-check the definitions in the syllabus glossary for these terms.
explanation.examTip: Test progress reports are periodic/interim; the test closure report is produced once testing activities are complete.

questions.scenarioText: With the planned release date approaching, a test progress report shows that only 60% of planned high-risk test cases have been executed, and several high-severity defects remain open and unresolved.
questions.questionText: A project is nearing its planned release date, but the test progress report shows only 60% of planned high-risk test cases executed, with several high-severity defects still open. What is the MOST appropriate use of this information?

options.text: Ignore the report and release on schedule regardless of test status
Use the report to inform a data-driven decision about whether to delay release, reduce scope, or allocate more testing resources
Immediately fire the test team for being behind schedule
Discard all remaining test cases to save time

explanation.correct: Test progress reports exist to provide objective information for stakeholders to make informed decisions, such as adjusting scope, schedule, or resources based on risk and status.
explanation.incorrect: Ignoring the data, taking punitive action, or discarding remaining tests all contradict the purpose of risk-based, informed decision-making that test reporting supports.
explanation.examTip: This is a classic example of testing 'providing information for decision-making' â€” one of the core testing objectives.

questions.questionText: Arrange the following test management activities in the general order they occur within a single test level.

orderItems.text: Test monitoring and control begins alongside execution

explanation.correct: This is the standard sequence defined in the ISTQB CTFL syllabus.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus section describing this sequence.
explanation.examTip: While monitoring and control run continuously alongside other activities, this represents their typical starting sequence relative to the core test process.

questions.questionText: Drag each defect report field to what it primarily documents.

dragCategories.name: Describes how urgently/severely to treat it

dragItems.text: Steps to reproduce the failure
Actual result observed versus expected result
Severity level (e.g., critical, major, minor)
Priority level (e.g., high, medium, low)

explanation.correct: Each item belongs to its category as defined in the ISTQB CTFL syllabus.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus classification for these items.
explanation.examTip: Separate the 'what happened' facts from the 'how urgent/severe' assessment fields of a defect report.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a valid reason a small startup might choose NOT to invest in a dedicated test management tool early on?

options.text: Test management tools are illegal for small companies to use
The overhead of tool selection, licensing, and training may outweigh the benefit for a very small team and simple project
Test management tools can only be used by certified testers
Spreadsheets can never be used to track any testing information

explanation.correct: For very small teams or simple projects, the cost and effort of introducing a dedicated tool may exceed its benefit, at least initially â€” a valid context-based decision.
explanation.incorrect: The other options contain false or absolute claims not supported by the syllabus.
explanation.examTip: Tool adoption decisions should always weigh cost/effort against benefit for the specific context.

questions.questionText: Decide whether each statement about test tool categories is correct (Yes) or incorrect (No).

statements.text: A defect tracking tool is used to log, manage, and monitor the status of defects.
A test data preparation tool helps generate or select data used as input for tests.
A coverage tool measures how much of the code has been exercised by a set of tests.
All test tools require no configuration and work identically across every organization.

explanation.correct: Each statement is evaluated independently against the ISTQB CTFL syllabus definition.
explanation.incorrect: Review the syllabus definitions for the concepts referenced in the statements above.
explanation.examTip: Recognize the standard tool categories: test management, defect tracking, test data preparation, coverage, static analysis, and performance tools among others.

questions.scenarioText: A hotel booking system allows guests to cancel a reservation for free up to 48 hours before check-in, charges 50% of the booking cost if cancelled within 48 hours of check-in, and gives no refund if cancelled after the check-in time has passed.
questions.questionText: A hotel booking system allows guests to cancel a reservation for free up to 48 hours before check-in, with a 50% charge if cancelled within 48 hours, and no refund if cancelled after check-in time. Which technique is BEST suited to deriving test cases for this time-based cancellation policy?

options.text: State transition testing, modeling reservation states such as Active, Cancelled-Free, Cancelled-Charged, and No-Refund
Statement testing on the booking confirmation email template
Checklist-based testing of the website's color scheme
Use case testing focused only on the payment gateway integration

explanation.correct: This policy is naturally modeled as states (Active, Cancelled-Free, Cancelled-Charged, No-Refund) with transitions triggered by the cancellation event at different points in time â€” a strong fit for state transition testing.
explanation.incorrect: Statement testing addresses code structure, checklist-based testing of colors is unrelated to this business rule, and narrowly scoping to only the payment gateway would miss the cancellation timing logic itself.
explanation.examTip: When a policy depends on 'where you are' in a process combined with time-based triggers, consider state transition testing.
